title: Choose a quieter architectural world
question: Which theme feels most native to VIZ Creative? Every option preserves the initial site's structure, expanding hero, restrained type, scrollytelling, routes, and uncropped media.

options.label: Casting Room
options.lineage: plaster casting studios, formwork negatives, and sculptural prototypes
options.thesis: VIZ reveals the finished space the way a casting room reveals form: through mass, void, surface, and controlled light.
options.viewport: The initial expanding hero remains intact, held in a quiet plaster-white field with compact studio copy. Sections transition like positive and negative casts, while the renders remain the only saturated material.
options.risk: The sculptural restraint could feel cool if the copy and occupied scenes do not carry enough warmth.

raised.raise: The site's structure stays visible and every section opens fully instead of hiding behind decorative transitions.
Light changes pace the experience, but never recolor or obscure the original renders.
Alignment and spacing obey a disciplined modular system at every viewport.
Each major project gets one decisive held moment instead of a busy collage.

options.label: Model Room
options.lineage: architectural maquette studios, pin-up walls, and exhibition plinths
options.thesis: The site becomes a working model room where each render is a full-scale window into a project under consideration.
options.viewport: The original hero composition sits on a generous model-board ground with a compact title block and one warm marker. Scroll moves from the full moving image into pinned project moments and a clear four-stage process.
options.risk: Architectural model language is highly credible and flexible, but more familiar than the assigned casting-room world.

options.label: After Rain
options.lineage: blue-hour city photography, wet concrete, and warm inhabited windows
options.thesis: VIZ is experienced as a sequence of inhabited views emerging from a rain-dark city into first light.
options.viewport: The expanding hero remains the first event, surrounded by near-black concrete rather than navy. A restrained sequence of project views changes with scroll like a film edit; warm light marks the next action.
options.case: It identifies immediately with architectural visualization and creates cinematic scrollytelling, but its nocturnal exterior bias is narrower than VIZ's full interior-design practice.
options.risk: Too much night imagery would make the portfolio feel mood-led rather than project-led.

options.label: Exposed Binding
options.lineage: Coptic-bound books with visible chain stitching
options.thesis: Every project and service opens as a complete section while the site's connective structure remains visible.
options.viewport: The hero opens flat beside a visible section spine and counted project signatures.
options.case: The structure is honest, but the book metaphor identifies less strongly with spatial design than the casting and model-room worlds.
options.kept: Visible structure and sections that open completely.
options.risk: The studio could read as an editorial practice before it reads as an architecture practice.

options.label: Night Instruments
options.thesis: A fixed set of gauges turns every service into one measured project truth.
options.viewport: Six project signals surround a central moving render.
options.case: Its functional confidence is strong, but instrument-panel language is explicitly outside the desired theme.
options.kept: Each visible element owns one clear job and one state.
options.risk: It would repeat the distracting technical-overlay problem.

options.label: Pixel Arcade
options.lineage: CRT arcade screens and integer-scaled sprite grids
options.thesis: The portfolio becomes a precise luminous grid of scenes and states.
options.viewport: The hero resolves from coarse pixels into a full render.
options.case: The modular discipline is useful, but the visual language obscures the photoreal work and misidentifies the studio.
options.kept: A rigorous grid that scales without arbitrary breakpoints.
options.risk: The site would feel like an entertainment brand.

options.label: Surf Editorial
options.thesis: Project imagery and type collide into energetic editorial spreads.
options.viewport: Type crosses the render while fragments recompose on scroll.
options.case: It is intentionally chaotic and surf-coded, directly opposing the request for a quieter, more fitting theme.
options.kept: Every viewport should feel deliberately composed rather than merely stacked.
options.risk: The work would compete with its own interface.

options.label: Painted Hoarding
options.thesis: Each project becomes a single cinematic held moment.
options.viewport: One dramatic project image owns the frame before a hard cut to the next.
options.case: Its held-moment discipline is valuable, but the cultural and illustrative identity does not belong to the studio's actual work.
options.kept: One decisive project moment per section.
options.risk: It would turn the portfolio into a film-poster experience.

canonCard.label: Quiet Studio
canonCard.thesis: Keep the initial site's composition and motion, then replace the nautical palette with a neutral architectural studio system.
canonCard.viewport: The current expanding uncropped hero, compact navigation, and existing scroll chapters remain; color, typography, rules, buttons, and transitions are retuned to a calm studio language.
canonCard.risk: It is the least disruptive and most immediately credible option, but intentionally less distinctive than the committed worlds.
